{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Reduce forecast overshoots following sharp price spikes, especially when sentiment is neutral or negative.",
    "Adjust forecasts downward if sentiment turns negative (e.g., -0.25 or below) in the last 3–5 days, indicating bearish momentum.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.",
    "Increase downward bias when true outcome consistently underperforms forecast (e.g., >3 consecutive days of underperformance).",
    "Lag correction: if forecast is significantly ahead of true outcome (e.g., >15% over 3–5 days), reduce by 5–10% to account for lagged market reaction.",
    "Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment shifts — if sentiment changes from 0.00 to 0.50, adjust forecast only moderately unless price is already trending sharply.",
    "When sentiment is positive (0.50+), allow slight upward bias but cap at +5% above recent 7-day average to avoid overcorrection.",
    "If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3–5 days), apply a downward correction of 5–10% to reflect mean reversion."
  ]
}
